Identity.History: Pelopidas was one of the leading Theban generals and statesmen of the 4th century BC, remembered especially for helping overthrow Spartan control of Thebes in 379 BC and for commanding the elite Sacred Band. Alongside Epaminondas, he played a central role in Thebes’ rise to power, fighting successfully against Sparta and helping secure the decisive victory at Leuctra in 371 BC. Pelopidas also campaigned in Thessaly against the tyrant Alexander of Pherae and intervened in Macedonian affairs, where the young Philip II was reportedly among the hostages sent to Thebes. He was killed in battle at Cynoscephalae in 364 BC, charging aggressively against Alexander’s forces; although he died in the fighting, the Thebans won the battle and honored him as one of their greatest commanders.
